name: Barbell Bench Press
cue: Retract scapulae into bench; drive through heels and touch lower sternum before lockout.
why: The primary horizontal press — heaviest chest loading.
steps: Lie flat with eyes directly beneath the bar. Plant feet firmly flat on the floor with moderate arch.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width. Squeeze the barbell firmly to pre-engage lats and triceps.
Inhale deep into the diaphragm, brace abdominal core, and unrack with arms locked over upper chest.
Lower bar steadily (2–3 seconds) until lightly touching lower sternum with elbows tucked at 45–60°.
Drive heels down and press explosively up back toward eye line, exhaling past the sticking point.

name: Flat Dumbbell Press
cue: Keep wrists stacked over elbows; open the chest at the bottom.
why: Matches barbell chest activation with greater glenohumeral freedom and deeper stretch.
steps: Sit with dumbbells on thighs, kick them up one at a time and lie back with shoulder blades pinched.
Press both dumbbells over the chest with palms facing forward and a slight arch.
Lower for 2–3 seconds until elbows sit just below bench level, forearms vertical.
Drive up and slightly in, squeezing the chest at the top without clanking the weights.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
cue: Set the bench at 30° and keep ribs down.
why: Shifts load to the clavicular fibers while keeping equal pressing volume.
steps: Raise the bench to 30°. Higher angles turn the lift into a shoulder press.
Sit back, pin shoulder blades, and press the dumbbells to arm's length above the upper chest.
Lower under control until the elbows are about 45° from the torso.
Press back up along a slight arc, finishing with biceps close to the ears.

name: Plate-Loaded Chest Press
cue: Seat height so handles line up with mid-chest.
why: Zero stabilizer fatigue. Allows training to true muscular failure safely if solo.
steps: Set the handles level with mid-chest and keep your back flat against the pad.
Hold the handles with wrists neutral and shoulder blades retracted.
Push until arms are almost straight without shrugging.
Let the plates come back slowly until you feel a chest stretch.

name: Deficit Weighted Push-Up
cue: Body in one line from head to heels.
why: Ideal when benches are busy. Serratus engagement and deep pec stretch.
steps: Hands on blocks or plates, a little wider than shoulders, feet hip-width.
Squeeze glutes and abs so the body forms one straight line.
Lower the chest between the hands until it passes hand level.
Press the floor away and finish with shoulder blades wide.

name: Standing Cable Chest Fly
cue: Soft elbows; hug a barrel.
why: Constant cable tension finishes the chest without loading the shoulders.
steps: Place both pulleys at shoulder height and step forward into a split stance.
Start with arms wide, elbows slightly bent, chest proud.
Bring the handles together in a wide arc in front of the sternum.
Squeeze for a beat, then return slowly under tension.

name: DB Overhead Shoulder Press
cue: Squeeze glutes; avoid hyperextension.
why: Vertical press with a free path for the shoulder joint.
steps: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows slightly forward, ribs stacked over hips.
Squeeze glutes and exhale to lock the core before pressing.
Press up and slightly in until arms are straight over the shoulders.
Lower to ear level under control and repeat without leaning back.

name: Standing Barbell Press
cue: Push your head through once the bar passes the forehead.
why: Heavy vertical strength driver.
steps: Hold the bar just outside the shoulders, elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Squeeze glutes, tuck ribs and keep the forearms vertical.
Drive the bar straight up, moving the head back then through.
Finish with the bar over mid-foot, shrugging lightly overhead.

name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
cue: Pin elbows tight, peak lockout hold.
why: Direct triceps volume with constant tension.
steps: Stand close to the high pulley with a slight forward lean and elbows glued to your sides.
Hold the bar or rope with wrists neutral.
Push down until the elbows are fully straight.
Return slowly until forearms are just past parallel.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
cue: Hinge deep, pull to lower ribcage.
why: The primary horizontal pull for back thickness.
steps: Push hips back until the torso is near 45° with a flat spine and soft knees.
Hold the bar just outside the knees with an overhand grip.
Drive elbows back and pull the bar toward the lower ribcage.
Lower under control until arms are straight without rounding the back.

name: Seated Cable Row
cue: Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
why: Supported pull that keeps lower back fatigue low.
steps: Plant feet, soften knees, and sit with a long spine and arms extended.
Pull the handle to the navel while squeezing shoulder blades together.
Hold for one beat with the chest proud.
Let arms extend slowly and reach slightly for a full stretch.

name: Lat Pulldown
cue: Pull elbows to back pockets.
why: Vertical pull for lat width when pull-ups are not an option.
steps: Secure thighs under the pad and grip the bar just wider than shoulders.
Lean back slightly with the chest lifted.
Pull the bar to the upper chest, driving elbows down and back.
Return the bar slowly until arms are fully extended.

name: Pull-Up
cue: Start each rep by pulling the shoulders down.
why: Bodyweight vertical pull — no machine needed.
steps: Grip the bar just wider than shoulders and hang with active shoulders.
Pull shoulder blades down and back before bending the elbows.
Drive the chest toward the bar until the chin clears it.
Lower for 2–3 seconds to a full hang.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
cue: Keep the torso still; row to the hip.
why: Unilateral pull that fixes left-right imbalances.
steps: Place one hand and knee on a bench with a flat back.
Let the dumbbell hang with the shoulder blade protracted.
Pull the elbow toward the hip, not straight up.
Lower to full stretch before the next rep.

name: Romanian Deadlift
cue: Push hips back; keep the bar dragging along your thighs.
why: Posterior-chain loading with a long hamstring stretch.
steps: Hold the bar at hip level, feet hip-width, knees softly bent.
Push hips back and slide the bar down the thighs with a flat back.
Lower until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, usually just below the knees.
Squeeze glutes and drive hips forward to stand tall.

name: Barbell Back Squat
cue: Knees track over toes; chest stays proud.
why: The foundation lower-body strength lift.
steps: Set the bar across the upper back and unrack with a tight brace.
Sit between the hips until thighs are at least parallel.
Push the floor away and stand up with the chest up.

name: Goblet Squat
cue: Elbows inside the knees at the bottom.
why: Easy-to-learn squat with a built-in counterbalance.
steps: Cup one dumbbell vertically at the chest.
Sit straight down, elbows tracking inside the knees.
Hold the bottom for a beat with an upright torso.

name: Leg Press
cue: Do not let the lower back peel off the pad.
why: High-volume leg work without spinal loading.
steps: Feet shoulder-width on the platform, back flat on the pad.
Release the safeties and hold the sled with knees soft.
Bring knees toward the chest until just before the pelvis tucks.
Press through the whole foot without locking the knees.

name: Forearm Plank
cue: Ribs down, glutes tight, breathe slowly.
why: Anti-extension core stability.
steps: Place forearms on the floor with elbows under shoulders.
Extend legs and form one line from head to heels.
Tuck ribs down and squeeze glutes.
Breathe through the nose and hold without sagging.

name: Cable Crunch
cue: Curl the ribs toward the pelvis; hips stay still.
why: Loaded spinal flexion for the abs.
steps: Kneel under a high pulley holding the rope beside the head.
Curl the spine, bringing elbows toward the knees.
Hold the contraction for a beat.
Come back up slowly, keeping the hips fixed.
